question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed shared localization runtime and its five-PR landing sequence before reviewing this cumulative runtime-adoption slice for merge?
rationale: This PR introduces a cross-product localization contract and depends on an open foundation PR; code review cannot determine whether that permanent product and ownership direction should be accepted.

options.title: Accept the staged localization direction
options.body: Land the foundation after owner review, then require this PR to rebase as the narrow CLI/runtime adoption slice with exact-head proof.

options.title: Request a narrower proposal
options.body: Ask the contributor to split the operator-output adoption from shared protocol, coverage, and cross-product runtime design work.

options.title: Decline the core runtime direction
options.body: Keep current surface-owned localization approaches and close the cumulative series rather than introducing the shared contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the staged localization direction
recommendation.body: Land the foundation after owner review, then require this PR to rebase as the narrow CLI/runtime adoption slice with exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked RFC-backed localization series and can clarify the intended contract and slice boundaries for maintainer consideration.
